items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: This boy that Cootie and Sid and I had hired to drive us to work every night

ctx.x: One night, he looks down, and Ziggy is standing right in front of him. He see Ziggy standing there and he say, "Pht." Like he's spitting in Ziggy's face. So he comes to me one night, and he says, "There's no point in -- I'm going to try someone else." He says, "There's no point in me dragging you and you dragging me." I said, "Okay." So the next night, I come to work, he had Marty Blitz there. Marty had just left Claude Thornhill's band. Marty's a good bass player.

So I went out in the car to listen to the broadcast. This boy that Cootie and Sid and I had hired to drive us to work every night, the driver say, "I've never worked for Benny. If I had to drive for him, and he says turn here, he'd probably tell me to turn in the middle of the block."

So we listened to this broadcast, we can't hear nothing but bass. Thumping, you know. So I overheard someone say, "How do you like the new bass player." Say, "He's all right, but I'll straighten him out." Marty stayed with the band two weeks. (laughs)
